rationale: A wins because it respects the shape of the facts and forces the ugly proof questions before anyone hits send. Its line, "What does 'default' mean operationally (auto-substituted, first listed, no upcharge)," is exactly the question that keeps a trade pitch from face-planting. B has usable pieces, but "One coffee chain just made dairy optional. Dairy is taking notice." invents both a dairy displacement and an industry reaction; that is not a lens, it is a liability.
gaps_in_A: "Oatly launches its lowest-footprint product while closing a US plant" overclaims the update; 31% lower than the old formula is not proof this is Oatly's lowest-footprint product.
"The closure is underway now" adds execution timing the update does not give; 'is closing' is current, but the local labor angle needs the actual date before calling the clock.
"Five viable shapes exist" counts a defensive-comment posture beside pitchable angles; useful, but it muddies the next step because that worker/community item is explicitly not outreach.
gaps_in_B: "made oat milk the default, not the option" and "switch away from dairy" misread the central fact; Oatly became the default non-dairy option, not the default milk.
"When oat milk stops being the alternative and becomes the default pour" repeats the same overreach and tries to build a category story on one chain before it has proof.
"One coffee chain just made dairy optional. Dairy is taking notice." invents both dairy becoming optional and an incumbent reaction; the update gives neither.
"Oatly holds the line on price while going greener" — `duplicate` wrongly discards one of the cleanest distinct angles: verified footprint reduction with no retail price change.
